Frame.reason: The class of every scene's camera, `this.frame`, which `s.focus` moves: a camera helper or an author's test names it as a type, and a scene drawn without a stage moves it directly. A scene on a stage moves the camera with `s.focus`, which keeps the heading on screen, never with `this.frame.animate`. 0.1.0 published it.

MathTex.check: Glyphs: a formula the lettering snapshot does not hold fails every command

Mobject.check: Keys: two parts on the stage with one key at the end of a step fail

Scene.check: Seek, Trace, Hold, Last frame: every scenario is played and seeked; a seeked frame or trace that differs from the played one, a picture that changes after its caption's hold begins, or a step that ends on a different picture from its last frame, fails

Text.check: Text, Legibility, Glyphs: native text that overlaps other text, reads under 14 px at 1280 px, or has characters the fonts cannot draw fails

Transform.check: Motion: a part that pops, cuts in or out, or teleports fails

TransformMatchingShapes.check: Motion: a part that pops, cuts in or out, or teleports fails

TransformMatchingText.check: Motion: a part that pops, cuts in or out, or teleports fails

keyed.check: Keys: two parts on the stage with one key at the end of a step fail

matchByKey.check: Keys: two parts on the stage with one key at the end of a step fail

Diagram.check: Routes over labels, Legibility: an imported connector over label ink, or an imported label under 14 px in its viewport, fails

stage.check: Words, Step change: a kept drawing with no text and no describe, or a step whose resting picture equals the previous step's, fails

having.check: Views: a draw that reads a state of another shape throws, which counts as reading its state, so a draw that narrows with having is held to the state it draws

Machine.check: Machines: every state its events reach is drawn and fails if it collides, has a label under 14 px, has no description, does not show its state or is described like another

refuse.check: Machines: a bound that stops an event the model refuses anyway fails

view.check: Views: at the end of every step, a view whose words, parts, boxes or opacity differ from a fresh draw of the state, placed where a sync would put it, fails

palette.reason: A named style's four colours, so a scene can start from a style and change one of them (`{ ...palette('dusk'), accent }`), which the stage's `style` option cannot; the stage resolves its own `style` with it. 0.1.0 published it.

card.check: Views: a card drawn from state is compared part by part, its lit row included, with a fresh draw

code.check: Views: a code panel drawn from state is compared part by part, its lit bar included, with a fresh draw

keyedParts.check: Keys: two parts on the stage with one key at the end of a step fail

legend.check: Looks: a caption or line naming a colour or pattern that no word on the stage says fails; a legend that keys the look answers it

table.check: Keys: two parts on the stage with one key at the end of a step fail

depthOrder.check: Invariants: registered with addInvariant, it fails on the first frame that draws a piece out of depth order

DomSink.tooling: a host page written against 0.1.0 that plays a scene into its own live SVG element, until 0.3.0; deprecated: 0.1.0 published it from rayner, no explainer uses it, and 0.3.0 removes it. The player's zoom view keeps it from the repository's own path

NullSink.tooling: a test or tool written against 0.1.0 that runs a scene for its state, steps or invariants and draws nothing, until 0.3.0; deprecated: 0.1.0 published it from rayner, no explainer uses it, and 0.3.0 removes it. rayner check and the repository's tests keep it from the repository's own path

StopScene.tooling: a host page or tool written against 0.1.0 with its own sink, which throws it to stop a run and must rethrow it from a catch, until 0.3.0; deprecated: 0.1.0 published it from rayner, no explainer uses it, and 0.3.0 removes it. The player keeps it from the repository's own path

StringSink.tooling: a tool that collects every frame of a run as SVG strings (the render recipe)

renderFrame.tooling: a host page or tool that draws a step's resting picture, or any frame, by the frame number a trace records (the player, the build's poster and rayner check's seeks)

renderElements.tooling: a tool written against 0.1.0 that reads a frame as element records, with each part's box, paint and text (the render recipe), until 0.3.0; deprecated: 0.1.0 published it from rayner, no explainer uses it, and 0.3.0 removes it. rayner check and review keep it from the repository's own path

renderText.tooling: a tool or test written against 0.1.0 that prints a frame as a text drawing, for a terminal or a reviewer (the render recipe), until 0.3.0; deprecated: 0.1.0 published it from rayner, no explainer uses it, and 0.3.0 removes it. rayner describe and see keep it from the repository's own path

toSvgString.tooling: a host page or tool that serializes the scene's current picture as one SVG document, such as a step's still from the scene renderFrame returns (the render recipe)

InvariantSink.tooling: an author's test that checks every frame of a run against the scene's invariants (the invariants recipe)

TraceSink.tooling: an author's test or tool that records each step's timing, state and evidence while it runs a scene its own way

describeExplainer.tooling: an author's tool or agent that reads the explainer as one JSON object: scenarios, steps, state and pictures in words

assertStepState.tooling: an author's test that compares each step's state with the program the explainer explains (every explainer's fidelity check)

assertSteps.tooling: an author's test that names the steps it reads, in order, so it survives an edit to the rest of the story

assertViewFollowsState.tooling: an author's test that checks a view shows the traced state at the end of every step (ring-buffer, henge and five more)

diagramFindings.tooling: an author's test that reads the verifier's warnings on a pinned diagram snapshot without building its diagram

diagramOf.tooling: an author's test that reads a pinned diagram's words or parts (pg-page, traffic-policy, gnome-files, tailwind-gamut and gtfs)

jsonObject.tooling: an author's test or tool that validates and clones state under the trace's JSON rules (the document recipe)

loadFonts.tooling: an author's test or tool that draws text outside a scene's run, and so loads the embedded fonts first

loadProject.tooling: an author's test that runs every scenario of an explainer from its folder, with its script's intent and pinned snapshots, as the command does

loadSnapshots.tooling: an author's test or tool that reads an explainer's pinned diagram snapshots from its folder, to build or inspect one diagram

pictureWordsAt.tooling: an author's test that reads what a reader who cannot see the stage is told about a step's picture

sampleAnimation.tooling: an author's test of a custom animation that draws its frames at chosen alphas, in any order (the continuous recipe's test)

traceScene.tooling: an author's test that compares a run's steps and state with the model (the render and document recipes)

withIntent.tooling: an author's test that runs a scene directly with its script's intent adopted, as the command runs it

withSettings.tooling: an author's test or tool that runs a scene in one scenario of its settings

features.uses: `TransformMatchingText`, `TransformMatchingShapes` (`shapeKey()`), `TransformMatching` with your own key or `matchByKey()` (keyed components); `summary()`, `pairs`, `removed`, `added`
`new TransformDiff(before, after, { hunks })` and its `plan`; `diffLines`, `parseUnifiedDiff` for hunks

features.feature: Parts of a line of code

examples.explaining: Two algorithms or policies on the same input
examples.shows: One card with a column per policy, read from the model's trace; one scenario that favours each policy; captions tested against the model

examples.explaining: A code change and what it does to a system
examples.shows: `TransformDiff` on the code, the same edit replayed on the diagram with `ops`, a setting for hit or miss

examples.explaining: A protocol or request flow
examples.shows: A sequence diagram revealed message by message (`build: 'frame'`, `reveal`); a setting that adds the attacker's step

examples.explaining: A sequence of separate pictures, one per step
examples.shows: `s.steps([...])`: each step carries its `state` and a `draw(state, s)` for its picture; `rayner check` redraws every step after the run and fails one that comes out different

examples.explaining: A data structure changing step by step
examples.shows: No diagram: native shapes drawn as views of `scene.state`, a `Machine` of push and pop, each event's motion authored with the transition's `t.choreograph`, `c.follow` for the pointers

examples.explaining: A state machine
examples.shows: A state diagram driven as a `Machine` by a model run against the real client (Node’s WebSocket), and code spans of its real `send()` boxed from the branch it ran

examples.explaining: A model the reader could drive with events
examples.shows: A `Machine` over the model's step, refusals with reasons, a live last step; `rayner check` draws every reachable state

examples.explaining: Nested or parallel states
examples.start: A Mermaid `stateDiagram-v2` with composites and regions ([recipe](../../docs/REFERENCE.md#state-machines-and-graphs)); `statecharts` when position carries meaning
examples.shows: `statecharts`: native boxes and arrows drawn from a model's states and transitions; a keyed `view` whose parts keep their identity as a grid becomes regions; a flat and a structured drawing side by side

examples.explaining: A race or ordering bug
examples.shows: A real controlled-promise run that opens on the unguarded race (the page ends on the older query) before naming the ticket that fixes it; guard and completion order change the displayed result

examples.explaining: A rate or a model's numbers over time
examples.shows: `token-bucket`: `Axes`, `lineGraph`, `g.follow` for the gauge and the line from one elapsed time; `seasons`: `Axes.plot`; a setting that reruns the model

examples.explaining: Identity, hashing or text that changes
examples.shows: `exgit`: Git's objects drawn as `view`s of the repository's state and synced as each command runs, a `BraceLabel` on the abbreviated id; `glyph`: `TransformMatchingShapes` pairs letters by their outlines

examples.explaining: Keyed cells or nodes rearranged between pictures of the same state
examples.shows: `view(...).sync()`, which matches by key; `matchByKey({ fallback })` for unkeyed parts that should stay put, `{ text: 'whole' }` when a relabelled part is a new thing (`statecharts`); `find(key)` to address a part

examples.explaining: A real tool's behaviour, checked against it
examples.shows: A model checked against the tool's own output, with a fidelity test

examples.explaining: Records, schedules or shares
examples.shows: Diagram families beyond flowcharts

examples.explaining: A subject in another language
examples.shows: `meta.lang: 'fr'`; descriptions in French

examples.explaining: A drawing made by hand, values said on it
examples.shows: `s.sketch` with a pen and pencil, `s.focus` on the camera, `s.carry`, the kit's `dimension` and `callout` instead of cards

examples.explaining: A claim about viewpoint or projection
examples.shows: `seenFrom` and a turned model from `rayner/geo`: 3D earns its place when the claim is about how a thing looks from somewhere (a straight line on a globe is curved on the map). Otherwise a 2D section in the right plane reads better, as `seasons` draws the Sun's rays

examples.explaining: A requested face in text and diagrams
examples.shows: EB Garamond, real cuts and `lettering: 'natural'` diagram measurements

examples.explaining: Sound compared with a visible score
examples.shows: Optional `step.audio`, two piano rolls from the played notes, an unchanged-timing control; see [score audio](../../docs/REFERENCE.md#optional-score-audio)

examples.explaining: Explicit panel placement and field order
examples.shows: RTL `start`/`end` placement, a card's LTR override and updates that keep their columns
